cards.interpretation: In AML, validated leukemia-specific MRD assays for NPM1, FLT3-ITD, PML::RARA, RUNX1::RUNX1T1, CBFB::MYH11, and KMT2A rearrangements are preferred over less-specific WT1 or MECOM expression markers.
cards.locator: C1. qPCR-based MRD assessment; recommendation C4

cards.interpretation: For NPM1-mutated AML qPCR MRD, negativity is defined as <0.001% mutNPM1/ABL1 or meeting EAC nondetection criteria with at least 10,000 ABL1 copies; BM levels are typically about tenfold higher than PB, so tissue-specific interpretation is required.
cards.locator: C1. qPCR-based MRD assessment — mutNPM1 MRD

cards.interpretation: After two chemotherapy cycles in NPM1-mutated AML, PB—not BM—is used for the formal qPCR MRD positivity definition; a positive PB result is classified as warning rather than high risk of treatment failure because the optimal postremission treatment remains uncertain.
cards.locator: C1. qPCR-based MRD assessment — mutNPM1 MRD after 2 cycles

cards.interpretation: In NPM1-mutated AML, ELN-defined molecular MRD relapse closely precedes clinical relapse and supports considering antileukemic therapy before morphologic relapse, with alloHCT also strongly considered.
cards.locator: A5. Clinical consequences of MRD assessment — mutNPM1 MRD relapse

cards.interpretation: In CBF-AML with RUNX1::RUNX1T1 or CBFB::MYH11, qPCR MRD is measured in bone marrow as CBF-mutant/ABL1 copies, with diagnostic baseline transcript quantification required. After two cycles of intensive chemotherapy or before alloHCT, a ≥3-log10 reduction from diagnostic levels is classified as an optimal response (MRD negative or low-level positive), whereas a <3-log10 reduction is MRD-positive and classified as warning.
cards.locator: Table 5. Response criteria for MRD monitoring — CBF-AML qPCR

cards.interpretation: For PML::RARA-positive APL, routine MRD testing is recommended at end of treatment rather than during treatment; end-of-treatment positivity is a warning, and follow-up monitoring is principally reserved for high-risk patients not treated with ATO, using BM because PB may become positive only near hematologic relapse.
cards.locator: C1. qPCR-based MRD assessment — APL-MRD

cards.interpretation: In FLT3-ITD AML, UHS-NGS MRD is recommended after two treatment cycles and before alloHCT; EOT and follow-up use rests on more limited evidence. Positivity is above the assay LOD, which must be at least 0.01%, and NPM1 may serve as the stand-alone marker when both mutations are present and FLT3 UHS-NGS is unavailable.
cards.locator: C2. NGS-based MRD assessment — FLT3-ITD

cards.interpretation: After alloHCT for FLT3-mutated AML, sorafenib maintenance is effective independently of pretransplant MFC-MRD status. Gilteritinib is recommended, on the basis of a MORPHO trial subgroup analysis, for patients with FLT3-ITD UHS-NGS MRD positivity before or around day 30 after alloHCT, particularly the reported subgroup with one FLT3-ITD MRD clone and mutated NPM1.
cards.locator: A5. Maintenance therapies; recommendation A15

cards.interpretation: In AML remission after intensive chemotherapy and before alloHCT, germ line mutations in predisposition-associated genes—for example ANKRD26, CEBPA, DDX41, ETV6, GATA2, RUNX1 and TP53—and mutations associated with age-related clonal haematopoiesis, such as DNMT3A, TET2 and ASXL1, are not prognostic and should not be used to determine MRD status at those time points.
cards.locator: C2. NGS-based MRD assessment — recommendation C13

cards.interpretation: After alloHCT for AML, serial UHS-NGS monitoring of diagnostic mutations can correlate with impending relapse even for predisposition- or clonal-haematopoiesis-associated genes, but NPM1 is specifically well validated and additional genes require rigorous posttransplant validation.
cards.locator: C2. NGS-based MRD assessment — recommendation C14

cards.interpretation: For AML MFC-MRD, the integrated LAIP/DfN strategy should include CD34, CD117, CD45, CD33, CD13, CD56, CD7 and HLA-DR; the recommended 10-color core and monocytic panels additionally specify CD38, CD11B, CD64, CD14, CD15, CD4, CD123 and CD36.
cards.locator: Table 2, recommendation B3

cards.interpretation: In AML, MFC assessment of CD34+/CD38− leukemia stem cells using aberrant CD45RA, CD123 and CLEC12A may add prognostic value beyond standard MFC-MRD; at least one million CD45-expressing cells supports higher-sensitivity measurement, but clinically actionable cutoffs still require validation.
cards.locator: B2. Quality requirements — leukemia stem cell MFC-MRD

cards.interpretation: In CEBPA bZIP in-frame–mutated AML, some evidence suggests that MFC-MRD is preferred after two cycles of intensive chemotherapy; its prognostic role at end of treatment and during follow-up requires further study.
cards.locator: B2. Quality requirements — CEBPA AML

cards.interpretation: In AML MFC-MRD, CD22- or CD15-associated abnormalities may reflect regenerating or stressed nonleukemic hematopoiesis rather than residual leukemia; reports should flag this possibility and consider repeat testing in 2–4 weeks when clinically indicated.

cards.interpretation: For residual TP53, IDH1, or bZIP-mutated CEBPA detected by UHS-NGS in AML, prognostic effects have not been demonstrated at selected pre-alloHCT time points; gene- and timepoint-specific validation is required before these findings are used as established MRD prognostic markers.

cards.interpretation: For ET, the authors proposed that a revised thrombosis-risk scheme might include four categories: very low risk, defined by no thrombosis history, age ≤60 years and JAK2-unmutated status; low risk, defined by no thrombosis history, age ≤60 years and JAK2-mutated status; intermediate risk, defined by no thrombosis history, age >60 years and JAK2-unmutated status; and high risk, defined by thrombosis history or age >60 years with JAK2 mutation.
cards.locator: Discussion: proposed revised four-category risk stratification

cards.interpretation: In conventionally high-risk ET, JAK2 mutation, cardiovascular risk factors, or both provided limited additional thrombosis-risk enhancement when high-risk status was defined by thrombosis history, regardless of age (P=NS). cards.locator: Additional analysis and discussion: high-risk status defined by thrombosis history versus age alone

cards.interpretation: Among conventionally assigned high-risk ET patients, annual thrombosis rates were 1.44% with neither JAK2 mutation nor cardiovascular risk factors, 1.64% with cardiovascular risk factors alone, 2.36% with JAK2 mutation alone, and 4.17% with both; the combined-risk group had significantly greater risk than patients with neither factor (P=0.011).
cards.locator: Results subsection (ii): conventionally assigned high-risk group

cards.interpretation: Pending prospective controlled studies, the authors would not insist on aspirin for very-low-risk ET (no thrombosis history, age ≤60 years and JAK2-unmutated) without cardiovascular risk factors, but advised once-daily aspirin when cardiovascular risk factors are present.

cards.interpretation: Pending prospective controlled studies, twice-daily aspirin may reasonably be considered, but is not mandated, for low-risk JAK2-mutated ET, particularly when cardiovascular risk factors are present.

cards.interpretation: Under the ICC framework used in this paper, recurrent AML-defining genetic abnormalities establish AML at 10% or more marrow or blood blasts, except BCR::ABL1 AML, which requires 20% blasts; PML::RARA, CBFB::MYH11, and RUNX1::RUNX1T1 are included among the 10% threshold abnormalities.

cards.interpretation: Variant translocations involving RARA, KMT2A, or MECOM are recognized as AML-defining entities; an in-frame CEBPA bZIP mutation, whether monoallelic or biallelic, defines the CEBPA-mutated AML subtype and is associated with favorable outcome.

cards.interpretation: A pathogenic TP53 mutation with variant allele fraction at least 10%, with or without loss of the wild-type allele, defines AML with mutated TP53; the paper describes these neoplasms as having a very poor prognosis.

cards.interpretation: In cases lacking TP53 mutation, pathogenic mutations in ASXL1, BCOR, EZH2, RUNX1, SF3B1, SRSF2, STAG2, U2AF1, or ZRSR2 classify AML as AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutations irrespective of prior MDS; these mutations confer adverse prognosis even in de novo AML.

cards.interpretation: The ICC classification is hierarchical. In the absence of an AML-defining recurrent genetic abnormality, AML with mutated TP53 takes precedence over AML with myelodysplasia-related gene mutations.

cards.interpretation: Germline predisposition should be considered in hematologic malignancy at any age, including older patients with possible DDX41 predisposition; confirmation should use nonhematopoietic material such as cultured skin fibroblasts, and only pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants are considered causative.

cards.interpretation: In the cohort used to develop IPSS-M, TP53 was encoded according to monoallelic versus multihit status. TP53 multihit was defined as multiple TP53 mutations or a TP53 mutation accompanied by loss of heterozygosity through chromosomal deletion or copy-neutral LOH.
cards.locator: Methods — Genomic Characterization; Results — Feature Encoding for IPSS-M Model Development

cards.interpretation: In MDS, TP53 multihit—but not monoallelic TP53 mutation—together with FLT3 mutations and KMT2A/MLL partial tandem duplication were the strongest adverse molecular predictors; FLT3 and MLL partial tandem duplication had the strongest associations with AML transformation.
cards.locator: Results — Association Between Gene Mutations and Clinical End Points

cards.interpretation: In MDS, mutations in ASXL1, BCOR, EZH2, NRAS, RUNX1, STAG2, and U2AF1 were independently associated with adverse leukemia-free survival, overall survival, and AML-transformation outcomes after adjustment for confounders and IPSS-R score.
cards.locator: Results — Association Between Gene Mutations and Clinical End Points

cards.interpretation: In MDS, DDX41 mutation was associated with higher marrow blasts and AML-transformation risk but favorable overall survival, particularly in MDS with excess blasts.
cards.locator: Results — Association Between Gene Mutations and Clinical End Points

cards.interpretation: In DDX41-mutated MDS, the observed clonal/subclonal architecture was suggestive of a germline variant followed by a somatic second hit; the study classified 87% of DDX41-mutated patients as carrying a likely germline variant, but this was not constitutional confirmation.
cards.locator: Results — Association Between Gene Mutations and Clinical End Points

cards.interpretation: In MDS, favorable outcomes associated with SF3B1 mutation were confined to the SF3B1a group, defined as SF3B1 mutation without isolated del(5q) or comutation with BCOR, BCORL1, NRAS, RUNX1, SRSF2, or STAG2. The favorable association was not observed in the SF3B1-5q or SF3B1b groups, including in low-blast disease.
cards.locator: Results — Association Between Gene Mutations and Clinical End Points

cards.interpretation: For MDS prognosis, IPSS-M assigns adverse main-effect weights to TP53 multihit, KMT2A/MLL partial tandem duplication, FLT3 internal tandem duplication or tyrosine-kinase-domain mutation, SF3B1-5q, NPM1, RUNX1, NRAS, ETV6, IDH2, CBL, EZH2, U2AF1, SRSF2, DNMT3A, ASXL1, and KRAS. SF3B1a is the sole favorable main-effect variable. The model also counts mutations in the residual genes BCOR, BCORL1, CEBPA, ETNK1, GATA2, GNB1, IDH1, NF1, PHF6, PPM1D, PRPF8, PTPN11, SETBP1, STAG2, and WT1. These residual genes were selected because they were not already individually modeled, occurred in more than 1% of the cohort, and had adverse effects of similar magnitude in univariable analysis. One residual-gene mutation therefore adds an adverse prognostic contribution, and two or more add a larger contribution; the model caps the residual count at two, so three or more residual-gene mutations receive the same residual weight as two. The residual count contributes to, but does not by itself determine, the patient's overall IPSS-M risk category.
cards.locator: Results — Feature Selection for IPSS-M Model Development

cards.interpretation: In MDS, 51 of 58 patients with KMT2A/MLL partial tandem duplication and 22 of 25 patients with FLT3 mutation—88% in each group—were upstaged from IPSS-R by IPSS-M.
cards.locator: Results — Restratification of Patients from IPSS-R to IPSS-M

cards.interpretation: In a correlative analysis of treated patients with MDS, TP53 multihit remained the strongest predictor of worse overall survival after hypomethylating agents, stem-cell transplantation, or lenalidomide.
cards.locator: Results — Relation Between IPSS-M and Treatment

cards.interpretation: In MDS, DDX41 mutation—although not selected for inclusion in IPSS-M—was associated with favorable overall survival after hypomethylating-agent treatment despite its association with AML transformation. The apparent specificity of improved outcomes with hypomethylating agents requires investigation in randomized studies.
cards.locator: Results — Relation Between IPSS-M and Treatment
